result.title: TOMAS: Topology-Aware Operation Modeling and Adaptive Staging for Egocentric Hand Forecasting
result.summary: Forecasting future hand movements from egocentric videos plays an important role in understanding human intentions and hand-object interactions. However, different manipulation intentions can lead to substantially different hand trajectories even when interacting with the same object. Existing methods have not sufficiently explored the intrinsic relationships between articulated hand movements and object semantics to capture such operation-dependent motion patterns. Therefore, we propose TOMAS, a topology-aware operation modeling and adaptive staging framework for egocentric hand forecasting. Specifically, we develop a topology-aware hand-object reasoning mechanism that associates hand skeletal structures and articulation dynamics with object semantics and spatial relationships to jointly infer potential interaction targets and latent manipulation operations. The resulting object-operation representations provide interaction conditions for future hand trajectory prediction, with supervision adapted to the annotations available in each dataset. Furthermore, we introduce an adaptive staging mechanism that organizes future hand movements into ordered latent stages with learnable temporal boundaries. Stage-specific geometric subgoals are then incorporated to guide trajectory refinement according to the underlying manipulation patterns. Experimental results on multiple publicly available benchmarks demonstrate that TOMAS achieves state-of-the-art performance in multi-dimensional and multi-target hand motion forecasting.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TOMAS，从第一人称视频预测未来手部运动：用拓扑感知的手-物推理把手部骨骼结构与物体语义、空间关系关联，推断交互目标与潜在操作类型，并以自适应分阶段机制将未来运动组织为带可学习时间边界的隐阶段，用阶段几何子目标精化轨迹。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「潜在操作类型 + 可学习边界的有序隐阶段 + 阶段子目标」可视为一种结构化的隐式推理状态分解，可能为 LVR 中阶段化 latent 状态、停止/边界决策与几何证据筛选提供概念线索，但属视频运动预测任务，需核查其隐变量是否真正承载推理并影响输出。
